reviews.title: Not useful
reviews.text:
The app flags MSG as bad even though the science is inconclusive, including one of the cited sources in the app. That made me doubt it. Then I looked at other products I’ve compared in the past, and it shows sugar as low impact for one product but flags another even the sugar is higher for the first. These apps are about trust, and unfortunately I’ve lost trust in the methodology.

There needs to be a user rating and / or user commentary to adjust for the automated rating that is biased based on the flawed methodology.

reviews.title: Irreführender Score macht Produktvergleiche praktisch wertlos
reviews.text:
Die Grundidee von Yuka finde ich gut. Die Bewertung von Zusatzstoffen macht den Gesamtscore aber teilweise absurd.

Ein konkretes Beispiel: Eine Mahlzeit mit vernünftigen Nährwerten – wenig Zucker, wenig gesättigte Fettsäuren, ordentlich Protein und Ballaststoffe – landet bei 48/100 „mittelmäßig“, weil sie Kaliumsorbat (E202) enthält. Yuka stuft diesen zugelassenen Konservierungsstoff als „riskant“ ein und deckelt dadurch offenbar den GESAMTEN Score bei unter 50.

Das ist für mich keine sinnvolle Verbraucherinformation mehr. Ein ernährungsphysiologisch deutlich schlechteres Produkt kann dadurch locker 65+ Punkte bekommen, solange es keinen von Yuka entsprechend eingestuften Zusatzstoff enthält. Was soll ich dann anhand der beiden Scores eigentlich vergleichen?

Noch problematischer ist die Darstellung: Der durchschnittliche Nutzer sieht „48/100“, „mittelmäßig“ und einen roten Hinweis „riskant“. Kaum jemand dürfte daraus schließen, dass hier nicht einfach das ernährungsphysiologische Gesamtbild bewertet wird, sondern Yuka bei bestimmten zugelassenen Zusatzstoffen ein eigenes, besonders strenges Vorsorgeprinzip anwendet, das den gesamten Score massiv begrenzt.

Wer Zusatzstoffe grundsätzlich vermeiden möchte, soll diese Information selbstverständlich bekommen. Aber bitte getrennt vom eigentlichen Nährwert-Score – oder zumindest optional abschaltbar.

Ich möchte in den Einstellungen sagen können: „Zusatzstoffe nicht in den Gesamtscore einrechnen.“ Dann könnte ich Produkte anhand

reviews.title: Misleading and small minded
reviews.text: First of all, this app is very misleading. On a scan, they flag ANY additives. When you click for further details, it shows that some of the additives are completely risk free. For people who just look at it once, they’ll think that there’s 6 additives when in fact 5 could be completely risk free. It also assumes you’re trying to lose weight by flagging calories. It doesn’t even seem to care the amount of an additive. 1 gram of a carcinogen is different than 1 pound of one. For instance: store bought strawberries are sprayed with a tiny amount of a carcinogen, but it’s so small that you’d need to eat an inhuman amount of strawberries to get a risk for cancer. “The dose makes the poison” —Paracelsus

reviews.title: Sadly no longer accurate
reviews.text:
I have really loved using this app, a real eye opener into what’s in our food.
Sadly it’s no longer valid, as it seems their scientific team aren’t yet aware of the dangers of the man made Folic Acid (not to be confused with natural folate), which currently being put en masse into our food chain in may countries all in lock step.
Why their scientific team aren’t yet aware I cant imagine, the information is readily available.

So currently most bread with Folic Acid is highly rated, while at the same time, anyone with cancer, or vitamin b12 deficiency, or a heart stent for example, for whom Folic Acid is dangerous and are advised to avoid it, can currently be told the foods containing it are great on the app.

So sadly this app is no longer fit for purpose in my humble opinion so for me its back reading labels until an app maker does the right thing and warns people of this nasty chemical additive.

If were being really sceptical, I might think somebody is ordering these type of app makers to keep quiet about Folic Acid, or even worse, giving them some financial incentive not to look at it.

reviews.title: Does not flag all harmful ingredients
reviews.text:
More and more I’m seeing organic products with low scores, while the mainstream brands have higher ratings even though they have worse ingredients. 
A good example is with toothpaste. Doesn’t even mention if a product contains fluoride which is disappointing and begs the question how many other harmful ingredients it turns a blind eye to. 

Yuka, don’t do this. Just give unbiased feedback on all the ingredients in a scanned product. We can look at the findings and decide for ourselves whether or not we deem it to be “safe and effective”. There’s no need to omit results and findings, especially on ingredients that are well known to be bad, such as fluoride. It just reeks of “the government owns our asses”.

reviews.title: Great potential, but only works 5% of the time.
reviews.text: Been a paid subscriber and using this for a while, but recently started looking for an alternative. These days it’s very rare that this apps works at all, it constantly glitches and needs reloading. It’s not very often you can get a signal in shops, but when u can the app usually still doesn’t work, offline mode is it a must, but that still doesn’t work at all anymore either. Almost every product seems to come up with ‘artificial flavours’ despite being free from artificial flavours. It’s all just getting beyond a joke now, its like you have to fight to try and use the app, which is the last thing you want to be doing in the middle of shop. Recently I’ve not been using this app at all as I’ve just completely given up with it, so I’ve just been stick to buying my usual food that I know is okay till I can find a decent alternative or they fix this app, which in unlikely given how long these issues have been going on for and have been getting worse, which is a shame as this app does have great potential.

reviews.title: mManque de transparence
reviews.text:
Depuis plusieurs versions Yuka vante les mérites d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité: le classement des meilleurs produits accessible aux clients qui ont un abonnement premium. Or, Yuka oublie de mentionner que cette fonctionnalité n’est disponible qu’aux USA et en France. Si vous vivez ailleurs vous n’y aurez pas accès  même si vous faites des courses en France ou aux USA. Il me semble d’ailleurs qu’on peut acheter des produits français en même temps n dehors de la france, n’est pas ? Sauf si Yuka veut mettre des barrière au commerce entre les pays comme le ferait Donald. Les utilisateurs non USA ou FR sont donc tous discriminés. Pourtant il me semble qu’on paie le même prix pour l’abonnement …. Ce manque de transparence (a aucun endroit on vous prévient que le classement est réservé aux USA et FR) vaut une seule étoile au classement de l’application.
Et malgré des promesses rien ne bouge depuis plus d’une année…

reviews.title: Wrong Info
